audit_findings.title: Operating trust income may have been purged as portfolio income
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed recognized trust income: $202.2 million preneed plus $111.1 million perpetual care, totaling $313.3 million; amount actually purged unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing operating trust distributions lowers normalized owner earnings without a corresponding bridge asset.
audit_findings.evidence: Investment earnings from these trusts are distributed to us regularly and recognized in current cemetery revenue.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that perpetual-care trust distributions fund cemetery maintenance and enter operating revenue. It does not establish which trust-income items the valuation purged. With total recognized trust income exceeding the $275.5 million anchor, even a partial erroneous purge could materially change value.
audit_findings.action: Trace every portfolio-income adjustment to the 2025 general ledger and restore the normalized after-tax portion of operating preneed and perpetual-care trust income; rerun all scenarios without adding restricted trust assets as excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Cemetery-property amortization breaks the pipeline's D&A classification
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed amounts: $219.654 million PP&E depreciation and amortization, $16.370 million intangible amortization, and $104.262 million cemetery-property amortization; valuation error unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incorrect classification can duplicate or omit noncash add-backs and can mismatch cemetery-property amortization with cemetery-development investment in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Cemetery Property Amortization or Amortization of Cemetery Property — The non-cash recognized expenses of cemetery property interment rights, which are recorded by specific identification with the cemetery property revenue for each contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that cemetery-property amortization is a separate, inventory-like cost tied by specific identification to property revenue. The supplied record does not prove the precise 2025 calculation error, but the prior-year control failures and the separately filed $104.262 million amount make the $275.5 million anchor unreliable until reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the 2025 owner-earnings schedule with separate controls for PP&E depreciation, finance-lease amortization, intangible amortization, and cemetery-property amortization; map each add-back to maintenance capex or cemetery-development cash outlay exactly once and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Recurring finance-leased asset replacement may escape maintenance capex
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed finance-lease asset amortization of $39.392 million and new finance-lease ROU assets of $46.049 million; 2024 and 2023 additions were $54.561 million and $58.791 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease asset amortization without deducting recurring replacement investment inflates owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Our finance leases primarily include transportation equipment but also include real estate and office equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate recurring finance-lease additions and amortization at a scale equal to 14.3% and 16.7% of the $275.5 million anchor, respectively. Whether the valuation already included a replacement allowance is unresolved, but omission is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the maintenance-capex workpaper for finance-lease ROU additions or an explicit replacement-cost proxy; if absent, add a normalized recurring replacement allowance and rerun all scenarios without treating ordinary debt principal as capex.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation claims and their COLI backing are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed deferred-compensation liability of $236.003 million, COLI cash-surrender value of $260.068 million, raw difference of $24.065 million, and $21.6 million of 2025 cash settlements
audit_findings.mechanism: Any realizable after-tax COLI asset or unmatched deferred-compensation liability changes the equity bridge; settlement timing can also affect normalized owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We paid $21.6 million of deferred compensation arrangements primarily associated with retired executives and other restructuring related charges during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Both omitted balances are demonstrated, but the raw $24.065 million net asset does not establish their economic offset. Only $30.8 million of COLI is explicitly linked in the filing to the $12.284 million supplemental retirement obligation; ownership, beneficiary matching, taxes, liquidity, and links to the larger deferred-compensation balance remain unresolved. The record therefore cannot establish the direction or materiality of the net adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a policy-by-policy reconciliation of COLI cash-surrender values, tax basis, loans, restrictions, beneficiaries, and related compensation obligations; determine whether the $21.6 million settlement was already captured in owner earnings, then rerun the bridge using only the realizable after-tax unmatched balance.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge exposure of $260.411 million, equal to $1.86 per share and 6.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Minimum operating, Canadian, or otherwise encumbered cash should not be added as distributable excess cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to cash balances residing in Canada and minimum operating cash requirements, a portion of our cash on hand is encumbered.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that some cash is encumbered, so treating every dollar as excess is not fully supportable. However, even removing the entire $260.411 million add-on would reduce bear, base, and bull values only to approximately $21.00, $27.72, and $32.71 per share, respectively, all far below the $82.21 market price. The maximum possible correction therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain treasury schedules separating minimum operating, Canadian, restricted, and freely distributable cash and correct the bridge for precision; no conclusion-changing rerun is required unless additional cash-like assets or liabilities are identified.

audit_findings.title: One-time headquarters spending may depress the 2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed headquarters spending of $69.898 million, equal to 25.4% of the $275.5 million owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Classifying a separately reported nonrecurring headquarters project as maintenance capex reduces anchor owner earnings and every scenario derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon completion of the new headquarters, the Company expects to monetize the existing corporate buildings, parking garage, and other land adjacent to the old headquarters buildings.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that headquarters spending was separately reported from $388.553 million of ordinary capital expenditures and financed through a dedicated construction facility. It does not establish whether the valuation deducted that separate line. If it did, the potential anchor distortion is large enough to materially affect value; future property-sale proceeds remain contingent and should not yet be credited.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $69.898 million headquarters line through the 2025 owner-earnings workpaper; if deducted as maintenance capex, remove it from the maintenance deduction and rerun all scenarios, while recognizing any old-headquarters sale proceeds only when realized and separately supported.
